key_insight: Human experts and LLMs can both generate viable synthesis recipes, but closed-loop experimental feedback is what enables discovery of new materials beyond known compounds.
engineering_relevance: A human-AI workflow can accelerate materials synthesis planning and reduce trial-and-error, making it useful for rapid exploration of complex chemical phase spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials using both humans and LLMs
Tested recipes in the lab and fed success/failure results back into the next round
Compared performance across two rounds for known vs. unknown targets
evidence_signal: Experimental success rates were similar for humans and LLMs on known materials (83% vs 75% in round one; 79% vs 71% in round two) but much lower on unknown materials, with one discovered new compound, Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Results are specific to the Ruddlesden-Popper / rock-salt perovskite space, so broader generalization to other chemistries or synthesis regimes remains uncertain.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
